Sampling-loop method and evidence

The timed batch calls FindTarget, Rescan, and TakeSample, then retains each complete thread record. It reuses cached file descriptors. CLOCK_MONOTONIC measures each batch. The loop has no sampling-frequency limit. Percentiles use nearest rank across all 3 repeats.

The continuous loop has different cache and scheduling conditions from the frequency-controlled sampler. The difference between these latency values and UDP delivery latency cannot be attributed to UDP alone. These values do not establish full sampler or collector capacity.

03 / Reproduce the result

Measured. Defined. Repeatable.

What ran

Host
Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9500 CPU @ 3.00GHz · 6 permitted logical CPUs
System
Linux 7.2.5-3-omarchy · x86_64
Target workload
1 busy native thread. The remaining 99, 299, or 499 threads wait on a condition variable.
Measurement window
3 × 30.0 seconds per case, after at least 5 seconds of warm-up. Frequency and thread count cases rotate across repeats.
Default auxiliary sampling
Resources every 5 seconds; memory maps every 30 seconds. status_fallback = false.

Repeat the matrix

make benchmark-sampler-matrix
cp build/sampler-benchmark.json docs/
python3 scripts/render_sampler_benchmark.py

The default matrix takes about 22 minutes. It writes all trials to JSON. The renderer updates this page and the README infographic from those measurements.

For a different duration, use python3 tests/benchmark_sampler.py --threads 100 300 500 --duration 60 --repeats 3. Add --output build/sampler-benchmark.json before rendering.

The matrix used two measurement sessions. An interrupted turn stopped the first session after 31 trials. The five missing trials resumed with identical sampler, workload, and driver hashes. Each trial retained its own warm-up and measurement window. The raw JSON records the interruption.

Metric definitions and measurement limits

Complete-sample latency

The sampler writes a real-time timestamp at the start of a thread tick. The receiver uses SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW to get each UDP packet’s kernel arrival time. Latency is the latest arrival across all chunks minus that tick timestamp. It includes thread discovery, /proc reads, packet encoding, and loopback UDP. It excludes receiver scheduling, JSON decoding, collector processing, disk writes, and resource or memory-map work after thread delivery. See the Linux timestamp documentation.

Percentiles and repeat variation

p50 is the median of all measured samples for a case. p95 is the nearest-rank 95th percentile of the same observations. Max is the slowest observed sample. The low-frequency cases have fewer observations. A p95 value is a measured tail statistic, not a latency guarantee or confidence interval. The help button next to the table shows the median range across trials for the selected case.

Delivered throughput

Thread records per second equals thread count × observed complete-sample frequency. Frequency uses the elapsed monotonic time between the first and last measured tick. A complete sample contains every expected target thread ID exactly once. This is delivered throughput at 1–10 Hz. The benchmark does not run the sampler without a rate limit, so it cannot establish saturation capacity.

CPU and resident memory

CPU uses the change in /proc/PID/schedstat execution time divided by monotonic elapsed time. 100% means one CPU core. RSS comes from /proc/PID/smaps_rollup, read once per second and at the end. MiB = 1,048,576 bytes. RSS excludes kernel allocations. CPU includes the default resource and memory-map sampling; thread-delivery latency ends before that work.

Scope and environment

These results apply to this host, build, and workload. The host runs a normal desktop; CPUs are not isolated and frequency is not fixed. Most target threads sleep. Results do not establish overhead for 500 CPU-bound threads, rapid thread creation, another host, a remote network, or the collector. Kernel arrival timestamps avoid receiver scheduling delay, but the receiver and desktop can still compete for host resources.

Loss and clock checks

The driver verifies all chunks, packet signatures, session continuity, exact target thread IDs, tick sequence, and tick spacing. It reads one complete sample beyond each measurement window to check the trailing boundary. A missing tick, incomplete sample, warning, or invalid clock measurement aborts the run. Real-time and monotonic elapsed times must agree within 0.1 ms across each run.

Source, build, and evidence

Sampler code is unchanged from PR #71. The benchmark driver adds thread-count coverage, latency timestamps, and checks across measurement boundaries.
